page: Vultr voc-m-16c-128gb-1600s-amd is an instance from the Optimized Cloud Compute family, tailored for memory-intensive enterprise workloads. It operates on dedicated AMD EPYC x86_64 processors clocked at 2.0 GHz, providing 16 virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores with two threads per core. The hardware architecture features 16 MB of L3 cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 KB of L1 data cache per core. Memory capacity is substantial, offering 128.0 GB of RAM configured at an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio (8.0 GB per core). Local storage is directly integrated, supplying 1600 GB of NVMe SSD capacity, alongside one complimentary public IPv4 address. The server operates without dedicated GPU acceleration.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate robust memory performance and solid CPU throughput. Stress-ng single-core execution registers in the top tier at 3207.88, while multi-core throughput achieves 50139.7 within the average range. Geekbench results include a single-core score of 1526.0 and a multi-core score of 11297.0, supported by clang compilation at 19388.0 and ray tracing at 23247.0. PassMark metrics reflect strong memory throughput at 2935.37, paired with a composite CPU score of 34978.34 and database operations testing at 7721.83. Memory bandwidth sustains 131.64 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 67.64 GB/sec for uncached large-block writes. Redis SET operations reach 30.71 million operations per second, and static web serving tests deliver 16.6 GB/sec throughput. Lightweight LLM inference runs capably on CPU, achieving 263.35 tokens per second on text generation using a 135M model and 20.15 tokens per second on a 7B model.

Hardware tradeoffs focus on significant RAM allocation and fast NVMe storage density rather than peak vector execution, as advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 are not present. Consequently, the voc-m-16c-128gb-1600s-amd delivers balanced cost efficiency for enterprise services requiring large working sets. It is well suited for in-memory caching platforms such as Redis, relational and NoSQL database engines, ETL processing pipelines, large-scale software builds, and high-concurrency web infrastructure.
description: Vultr voc-m-16c-128gb-1600s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance equipped with 16 dedicated vCPUs (8 physical cores) running on a 2.0 GHz AMD EPYC x86_64 architecture. Featuring a memory-optimized 8:1 ratio, it supplies 128.0 GB of RAM alongside 1600 GB of high-speed NVMe SSD local storage. In benchmark evaluations, it demonstrates top-tier single-core stress-ng performance and a strong PassMark memory score of 2935.37, complemented by solid memory bandwidth of 131.64 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 30.71 million Redis SET operations per second. Lacking dedicated hardware accelerators or AVX-512 extensions, the system prioritizes high memory density and local disk capacity over specialized vector compute. It provides cost-effective hardware utilization for in-memory databases, memory-bound caching layers, ETL workloads, and high-concurrency enterprise services.
